setup.zh: 树比外面高一倍，树皮黑得像铁。山涧边有鹿的蹄印，比你的巴掌还宽。
setup.en: The trees are twice as tall as outside, bark black as iron. By a stream, deer tracks wider than your palm.

recap.zh: 黑松岭深处，你们找到了一头大鹿的蹄印；你每一百步刻一道记号。
recap.en: Deep in Black Pine Ridge you found a big deer's hoofprints; every hundred paces you cut a mark.

zh: 松针厚如毯，踩下去无声。
山涧边，一行蹄印，比巴掌还宽。
en: Trees twice as tall, bark like iron.
Needles thick as a rug; no footstep sounds.
By the stream, hoofprints wider than a palm.

text.zh: 印子边上的泥还湿着，涧水正一丝丝渗进去——鹿过去，还不到一个时辰。
text.en: The mud at the print's edge is still wet, the stream seeping in thread by thread: the deer passed less than a watch ago.

text.zh: 蹄印到涧边一块青石前便断了；石上青苔刮掉两道，石头那边的软泥里，又是半个蹄印。
text.en: The prints stop at a grey stone by the stream. Two strips of moss are scraped off it, and in the soft mud beyond lies half a print.

text.zh: 涧边的枯草尖上挂着几根鹿毛，灰褐色，粗得像马鬃——好大一头鹿。
text.en: A few deer hairs hang on the dry grass by the stream, grey-brown and coarse as a horse's mane. A very big deer.

look_hint.zh: 蹄印在涧边断了。鹿总不会飞——你爹蹲在那儿不作声，等你看出个名堂来。
look_hint.en: The prints break off at the stream. A deer cannot fly — your father crouches there in silence, waiting for you to make it out.

story.zh:
黑松岭的树比外面的高一倍，树皮是黑的，摸上去凉冰冰的，像摸着一块铁；脚下的松针厚得像毯子，一脚踩下去，半点声息也无。他爹走在前面，这许多年来，头一回走得比儿子还轻。

晌午过后，两人在一处山涧边找到了蹄印。是鹿，一头大的，蹄印比小满的巴掌还宽，前山十年都没见过这么大的鹿。小满先看风——涧边的芦草尖儿齐齐往他们这边歪，风是从鹿那头吹过来的，它闻不着他们。

他爹瞧了一眼草尖，又瞧了儿子一眼，没有说话，小满却觉得他像是夸了自己一句。

他爹蹲在地下，摸着那个蹄印，手在发颤，低声道：「一张鹿皮……够交马家的租。剩下的肉，给你娘换一身新棉袄。给吴婆婆，送一条腿。再给阿禾家……赔一颗白菜。」说着抬起头来，冲小满笑了一下。自打马三走后，这是小满头一回见他笑。
story.en:
The trees of Black Pine Ridge stood twice as tall as those outside; their bark was black and icy to the touch, like touching a slab of iron; underfoot the needles lay thick as a rug, and a footfall made no sound at all. His father went ahead, and for the first time in many years walked more lightly than his son.

After noon, by a mountain stream, the two of them found hoofprints. Deer — a big one, prints wider than Xiaoman's palm; the front hills hadn't seen a deer that size in ten years. Xiaoman read the wind first — the reed tips along the stream all leaned their way; the wind blew from the deer toward them, so it couldn't smell them.

His father glanced at the reed tips, then at his son, and said nothing, yet Xiaoman felt as if he'd been praised. His father crouched and felt the hoofprint, his hand trembling, and said low: "One deer hide… that covers the Mas' rent.

The meat that's left, a new padded coat for your mother. A leg for Granny Wu. And for Ahe's family… a cabbage to make good." He looked up and gave Xiaoman a smile. It was the first time Xiaoman had seen him smile since Ma San left.

label.en: Follow the prints, a mark every hundred paces

exits.means: follows the deer tracks, cuts a mark every hundred paces, keeps the rules

story.zh:
蹄印往黑松岭的更深处去。两人又追了一个时辰，从断碑数起，小满一路刻了四十一道记号，刻得手指头都麻了。这一个时辰里，有两件事，他当时没有跟他爹说，后来也没有跟他娘说。

头一件是记号。刻到第二十几道的时候，他回头望了一眼，只见来路上那一溜树干上的刀口白生生的，一道一道排过去——排得不对。他刻记号是有规矩的，一律刻在树干朝着来路的那一面，好叫回来的人一眼便看得见。

可这一眼望过去，倒有两三道刻在了树的背面，冲着林子里头，倒像是刻给别的什么人看的。

他心里一跳，跟他爹说了一声「撒泡尿」，折回去十几步细看，那几道记号却好端端地刻在朝来路的那一面，刀口新鲜，树脂还在一丝一丝地往外渗，一点也没有错。他站在那里看了半天，终于决定：是自己眼花了。

饿的人眼花，这是常理，他饿了大半天，眼花一回，账上说得过去。可他回转身来，再往前刻下一道的时候，手按在树皮上，那树皮凉得像一块铁，他按了很久，才敢把刀落下去。

这一刀下去，「笃」的一声，过了一会儿，林子深处也「笃」的一声，隔得很远，慢了半拍，倒像前头还有一个人，也在树上刻记号。他停了手，那边也停了。他又刻一刀，那边隔了半拍，又是一声。

他站着听了片刻，心想，是回声，山里的回声，向来是这么慢吞吞的——只是他在蒙山爬了十二年的树，从没听见过哪一处的回声，是从前头传过来的。

第二件是鸟。进了岭子深处，林子里倒渐渐有了几声鸟叫，稀稀落落的，比外头的鸟叫得低，也叫得懒。

小满正想，有了鸟叫，这地方总算有几分像座山了，忽然从头顶上不知什么地方，传来一声长长的鸟啼，拖着一个尾音，又细又远，听在耳朵里，竟像是有个人在很远很远的地方，一声一声地喊：「……回来……」他爹登时站住了。

那一双听得见三里外獐子踩断枯枝的耳朵，这一回偏着头，听了很久很久。那声音叫了三声，便不叫了。他爹的脸色有点发白，过了好一会儿，才道：「山鹧鸪。叫起来像人。」小满道：「它叫的是什么？」

他爹道：「别听。山里有东西喊你，别应。」说完这一句，便低下头去，接着看那蹄印，再没有提起。小满也没有再问。他觉得他爹像是知道点什么，又觉得他爹其实什么都不知道，只是怕。他心里却忍不住想：要真是有人在喊，喊的是谁？

这林子里头，除了他和他爹，还有谁该回来？这念头一冒出来，他便不敢往下想了，把它和那两三道看错了的记号搁在一处，压在心底，压得严严实实。
story.en:
The hoofprints led deeper into Black Pine Ridge. They followed for another hour, and counting from the stele Xiaoman cut forty-one marks along the way, till his fingers went numb. In that hour two things happened that he didn't tell his father at the time, nor his mother later.

The first was the marks. Somewhere past the twentieth he looked back: the knife-cuts on the trunks behind them showed white, one after another — and they were wrong. He had a rule for marks: always on the side of the trunk facing the way they'd come, so whoever came back would see them at a glance.

Yet looking back now, two or three had been cut on the far side of the tree, facing into the forest, as if cut for someone else to read. His heart jumped. He told his father he needed to pee, went back a dozen steps and looked closely — and those marks sat plainly on the side facing the way they'd come, the cuts fresh, the resin still seeping out thread by thread, nothing wrong at all.

He stood looking a long while and finally decided his eyes had played a trick.

A hungry man's eyes play tricks; he'd been hungry half the day; one trick of the eye was fair on the books. But when he turned and went to cut the next one, his hand on the bark — the bark cold as iron — he held it there a long time before he dared bring the knife down.

*Tok*, went the knife, and after a moment, from deep in the forest, *tok* — far off, half a beat late, as though someone up ahead were cutting marks on a tree too. He stopped; it stopped. He cut again; half a beat later, another.

He stood and listened a moment and told himself: an echo; echoes in the mountains are always this slow. Only he had climbed Mount Meng's trees for twelve years and never once heard an echo that came from ahead.

The second was the birds. Deep in the ridge a few birds began to call again, thin and sparse, lower than birds outside, and lazier. Xiaoman was just thinking that with birdsong the place at last felt a bit like a mountain, when from somewhere overhead came one long cry with a trailing note, thin and far, and in his ears it sounded exactly like someone, very, very far away, calling over and over: "…come back…" His father stopped dead.

Those ears that could hear a river deer snap a twig three li away tilted and listened for a long, long time.

It called three times and fell silent. His father had gone a little pale, and only after a good while said, "Mountain partridge. Sounds like a person." Xiaoman said, "What's it calling?" His father said, "Don't listen. If something in the mountains calls you, don't answer."

He said that one thing, bent back to the hoofprints, and never mentioned it again. Xiaoman didn't ask again either. He felt his father knew something — and felt, too, that his father knew nothing and was only afraid. Still he couldn't help wondering: if someone really was calling, who were they calling?

In this forest, besides himself and his father, who else ought to come back? The moment the thought rose he didn't dare think further, and pressed it down in his heart beside the two or three misread marks, pressed down tight.

refuse.zh: 蹄印到涧边就断了，往哪儿追？先看清楚。
refuse.en: The prints stop at the stream. Follow them where? Look first.
